explanation.text:
(Pro. 11:1-31)

(Compare Margin). The Hebrews used stones for weights.

just--complete in measure.

bsb.text: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.

explanation.text: Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare Pro 16:18; Pro 18:12).

bsb.text: When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.

explanation.text:
guide--to lead, as a shepherd (Pro 6:7; Psa 78:52).

perverseness--ill-nature.

destroy--with violence.

bsb.text: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:2).

wrath--that is, of God.

bsb.text: Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.

explanation.text: direct--or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain (Pro 13:17).

bsb.text: The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.

explanation.text: deliver them--that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings (Pro 5:22; Psa 9:16).

bsb.text: The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.

explanation.text:
expectation . . . perish--for death cuts short all his plans (Luk 16:25).

hope of unjust--better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare Isa 40:29, Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.

bsb.text: When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.

explanation.text: Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare Pro 11:6).

bsb.text: The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 35:16; Dan 11:32). The just is saved by superior discernment.

bsb.text: With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.

explanation.text: The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

bsb.text: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.

explanation.text: By the blessing--implying active benevolence.

bsb.text: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.

explanation.text:
despiseth--or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise.

holdeth his peace--as if neither hearing nor telling.

bsb.text: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.

explanation.text: tale-bearer--(Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.

bsb.text: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.

explanation.text:
counsel--the art of governing (Pro 1:5).

counsellors--literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.

bsb.text: For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 6:1).

suretiship--(Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.

bsb.text: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.

explanation.text: retaineth--or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.

bsb.text: A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.

explanation.text:
merciful--kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare Pro 24:5), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others.

flesh--that is, his body, by penuriousness (Col 2:23).

bsb.text: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.

explanation.text:
a deceitful work--or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away (Pro 10:2; Pro 23:5).

sure reward--or, "gain," as from trading (Hos 10:12; Gal 6:8-9).

bsb.text: The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.

explanation.text: Inference from Pro 11:18 (compare Pro 11:5-6; Pro 10:16).

bsb.text: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:5).

froward--as in Pro 2:15, opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright.

in their way--or, "conduct."

bsb.text: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.

explanation.text: The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship (Psa 37:25-26).

bsb.text: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.

explanation.text: Jewels were often suspended from the nose (Gen 24:47; Isa 3:21). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.

bsb.text: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:28).

wrath--is that of God.

bsb.text: The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.

explanation.text: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pro 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

bsb.text: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.

explanation.text:
liberal soul--(Compare Margin).

made fat--prospers (Pro 28:25; Deu 32:15; Luk 6:38).

watereth . . . watered--a common figure for blessing.

bsb.text: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

explanation.text:
Another example of the truth of Pro 11:23; the miser loses reputation, though he saves corn.

selleth it--that is, at a fair price.

bsb.text: The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.

explanation.text:
good [and] mischief--that is, of others.

procureth . . . seeketh--implying success.

bsb.text: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:15; Psa 49:6; Ti1 6:17).

righteous . . . branch-- (Psa 1:3; Jer 17:8).

bsb.text: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.

explanation.text:
troubleth--as Pro 15:27 explains, by greediness for gain (compare Pro 11:17).

inherit . . . wind--Even successful, his gains are of no real value. So the fool, thus acting, either comes to poverty, or heaps up for others.

bsb.text: He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.

explanation.text:
a tree of life--Blessings to others proceed from the works of the righteous (Pro 3:18).

winneth souls--(Compare Margin) to do them good as opposed to Pro 6:25; Eze 13:18 (compare Luk 5:10).

bsb.text: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.

explanation.text:
Behold--Thus calling attention to the illustrations (compare Pro 11:23), the sentiment of which is confirmed even in time, not excluding future rewards and punishments.

bsb.text: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
